description: Whether an MCP server's toolset changed recently. Get recent history for one already-tracked MCP server on MCP Checkup, by "provider/name" ref (e.g. "acme/weather-mcp"). Events, newest first, up to `limit` results (default 20, max 50): `tools_changed` (at most one: when the set of tool names last changed); `tools_change_detail` (one per recorded tool-list change, the 10 most recent at most, whether names, parameters or descriptions changed; `itemization` is "not_kept" for a change older than 30 days (its per-tool detail is not held), "unitemizable" when the stored lists cannot be compared tool by tool, otherwise "itemized" and `added`, `removed`, `parameters_changed` and `description_only` each give `names` (up to 10 tool names) and a `total`); `protocol_revision_changed` (the signed protocol_revision changed between runs whose probe offered the same revision, or because the server switched between the legacy initialize and server/discover handshakes); `probe_offered_revision_changed` (the revision our probe offered changed, with a `note`); and any recorded baseline-drift events. `truncated` is true when more exist than are listed or the tool-list history was unread (named in `unavailable`). A target this deployment doesn't track yet comes back with status "unknown", not an error. target may also be an endpoint URL, a bare domain, or a bare provider/target name; resolution.method reports which was used ("ref", "endpoint", "host", or "name"). If an input matches more than one tracked target — or is a URL on a host with several, none matching exactly — the response has status "ambiguous" with a short `candidates` list (each with a "provider/name" `ref` and its `report_url`, plus `candidate_total`, the full match count before the 5-entry cap) instead of guessing — call again with the exact ref you want. A URL matching only by host returns its target with `resolved_from`. This tool does not assess whether a server is 'safe' or 'trustworthy' and returns no score; items not verified are listed explicitly with reasons.

target.description: A tracked target as "provider/name", a full endpoint URL, a bare domain, or a bare provider/target name.

name: get_mcp_history
title: Get a server's recent changes
